transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Aisha (Meridian Head of Data), Tom (SRE), Priya (Security), Luis (Product)

Summary: kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate telemetry, benchmarks, and prompt storage/retention policies. Focus on verifying tail latency under production-like burst, options to avoid storing raw prompts, and confirming redact/transform strategy for PII.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I’m Maya, AE on the account, and Jared is our SE. we wanted to run through the POC goals, sizing, and specifically the prompt telemetry and retention constraints that Priya called out.
[00:23] Aisha: Yeah hi, thanks. we mostly want to prove two things: one, we can keep below our 200ms p95 for single-turn requests at our normal traffic, and two, that we never persist raw PII in logs. that second bit is non-negotiable.
[00:47] Jared: Understood. to clarify, is the 200ms p95 an end-to-end number from your application to response, or just inference time?
[01:04] Tom: it's end-to-end right now, but for the POC we can slice it — we want to see the inference tail contribution. so if Redwood shows ~120ms for p95 under our batch profile that would be great.
[01:22] Maya: Good note. For the POC we usually run a separation: network + app overhead vs Redwood runtime. Jared will set up a benchmark harness that lets us toggle batch sizes and the KV cache.
[01:40] Jared: Quick thing — when you say KV cache, are you using prefix caching heavily in prod? I saw some of your docs say you keep session history server-side.
[01:53] Aisha: We do. but we need the option to avoid storing user messages verbatim inside the model prefix cache for the pilot, or at least store only hashed tokens.
[02:06] Priya: Correct. And beyond hashing, we need server-side redaction for certain PII types. redaction must be auditable. We can't rely solely on client-side redaction.
[02:20] Maya: Good, that's in-scope. Redwood supports several patterns: client-side redaction before send, server-side regex-based redaction, and a prompt-minimization mode where we store only prompt fingerprints and deterministic paraphrases. We can show examples.
[02:38] Luis: Paraphrases — can you explain that? sounds like it might change model outputs.
[02:45] Jared: Yeah paraphrase mode means we transform original user text into a neutralized summary that preserves intent but strips names, identifiers. There's a tradeoff — some loss in fidelity. we'll show a few examples in the benchmark.
[03:01] Aisha: We also need to know about embedding and vector storage. some of our flows store embeddings derived from prompts for search — can those be retained while raw text is deleted?
[03:14] Jared: Yes — embeddings are a separate artifact. we can configure TTL per artifact type: raw prompts, response cache, embeddings. so you can set prompt TTL=0 (no storage) while embeddings TTL=90 days, for instance.
[03:28] Tom: And key management? we need KMS/HSM control for any persisted tokens or embeddings.
[03:35] Maya: Absolutely, Private deployments support customer KMS keys. even in hosted mode we offer envelope encryption with redwood-managed keys or BYOK via KMS integration. we'll include the exact options in the security doc link.
[03:51] Priya: There's also the question of telemetry: we want observability, but not at the token-level. we need metrics (latency, QPS, model version) and sampling for request traces, but no full prompt dumps unless explicitly allowed.
[04:05] Jared: We typically emit structured metrics and can enable request-level tracing at a hashed/pseudonymized level. there's an option to only log metadata: prompt length, bucketed token counts, model id, and a hashed prompt id.
[04:22] Aisha: Can you support an allowlist for debug logs? ie: only if we open a debug case do you keep the full prompt content, and it's time-limited and audited.
[04:34] Maya: Yes, that's a pattern we use in enterprise pilots. debug capture requires an explicit request, is logged in the audit trail, and auto-expires. We'll show the audit log sample.
[04:47] Luis: For metrics — what's your typical throughput per GPU for our model family? we're running a Llama-variant 13B float16, roughly similar to open models in your catalog.
[05:00] Jared: For a 13B float16 on A100-ish hardware, throughput depends a lot on sequence length and batching. for 128 tokens avg, expect around 8–12 rps per GPU single-request latency; with batching you can push more tokens/s but tail latency increases. we'll run a benchmark with your avg payload to get precise numbers.
[05:22] Tom: Our peak QPS is about 150 rps for the targeted endpoint, but traffic is spiky; sustained is 40 rps. how does Redwood handle burst?
[05:35] Maya: Redwood Dedicated offers burst capacity and configurable autoscale policies. For the POC we'll simulate spikes and verify graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model or queueing with SLAs.
[05:49] Priya: For compliance we need proof: can you produce a replayable benchmark log that shows p95/p99 and token counts and that redacted content never appears in stored logs?
[06:01] Jared: Yes we can produce redacted transcripts and hashed ids. our test harness will produce a compliance artifact: per-request meta plus a hash map so you can map anonymized ids back to original payloads on your side only.
[06:16] Aisha: Ok. timeline question: you mentioned a 6-week POC. can you break down milestones?
[06:25] Maya: Sure. Week 0: onboarding + infra prep. Week 1: baseline benchmarks with your sample workload (no redaction). Week 2: enable redaction/paraphrase modes and rerun. Week 3: integration with your KMS and retention settings. Week 4: spike tests and failure mode validation. Week 5: final tweaks and evaluation against success criteria. Week 6: wrap-up and decision.
[06:49] Tom: Who do we need on the calls for the bench run? I will be the infra lead but may need an engineer from Palo Alto to open ports for private deployment — that's TBD.
[06:58] Maya: For the benchmark run we want Tom (SRE), Jared (SE), and ideally your product owner (Luis) to validate output quality tradeoffs.
[07:09] Luis: Sounds good. One more question on prompt storage: could you implement a prompt-hash-only mode where we store only a salted hash to enable cache hits but not recoverability?
[07:22] Jared: Absolutely — salted hashing is an option. also a hybrid mode: store only n-gram signatures rather than full prompt; again tradeoff in cache hit rate. We'll include hit-rate estimates in the bench report.
[07:38] Aisha: For PII redaction, our legal team wants a catalog of redaction rules and a sample false-positive/negative rate. is that something you can share?
[07:49] Maya: We can provide the rule sets and a small evaluation against synthetic examples. we'll show the limitations and recommend human review thresholds for high-risk intents.
[08:04] Priya: Also need to confirm data residency — logs for EU users must remain in eu-west region for the pilot.
[08:12] Maya: Noted — we can pin region in the POC config. Redwood Private or Dedicated in-region options will be used.
[08:23] Tom: On the technical deep dive side, Jared, can you outline what we'll need to run the bench? docker images, sample scripts?
[08:32] Jared: We'll provide a benchmark repo: k6/gatling scripts for traffic generation, a simple harness that can run either against hosted endpoints or a self-hosted connector for private mode. also an orchestration script to vary batch size, temperature, and token limits.
[08:48] Luis: Will the harness include accuracy checks? we need a quality metric beyond latency — e.g., percent acceptable responses on a 5k prompt set.
[08:57] Jared: Yes, we'll add a pass/fail rubric and sample evaluation scripts — ROUGE/embedding similarity and a human spot-check workflow.
[09:08] Aisha: Let's talk about non-repudiation and audit logs — we need tamper-evident logs for any time debug captures are enabled.
[09:17] Maya: We can produce immutable audit entries with sequence numbers and KMS-signed attestations for debug captures. we'll include a sample chain-of-custody artifact.
[09:29] Priya: One more operational ask: retention TTLs must be configurable per route. for example, internal agents route can be TTL=7 days, but customer-facing routes TTL=0.
[09:41] Jared: That's supported via route-level policies. We'll include a sample config.
[09:48] Luis: Are there any features that are not supported in hosted mode that we should be aware of?
[09:54] Maya: The main differences are around BYOK/HSM and absolute network control. Hosted supports many compliance features but major enterprise-only options (full VPC peering into your network or on-prem air-gapped) are in Redwood Private/Dedicated. We'll call these out.
[10:09] Tom: Ok great. Can you also include an estimated cost model for the POC? we need to budget for GPU hours for bench.
[10:18] Maya: We'll include a cost estimate and a breakdown by experiment: baseline, redaction-enabled, spike test.
[10:25] Aisha: What constitutes success? I want explicit pass/fail criteria.
[10:30] Jared: Proposed success criteria: 1) p95 inference latency <= 200ms end-to-end (or <=120ms inference contribution) under baseline traffic; 2) No raw PII persisted in any logs during the POC; 3) Model output quality within X% (to be defined) of your current baseline on the sample set; 4) Autoscale and burst policies demonstrate graceful degradation under 2x peak traffic.
[10:56] Aisha: Good — we will sign off if those are met plus acceptable security artifacts.
[11:02] Maya: Great. We'll send the POC scope and the benchmark plan. any other questions?
[11:09] Luis: One small one — will you be testing quantized variants? we might want to compare 8-bit quant vs float16 for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[11:18] Jared: We'll include a quantization matrix: 8-bit, 4-bit where supported, and float16. quality vs tokens-per-second will be in the report.
[11:28] Priya: Please note our regulatory window for review is two weeks after the POC ends. so timeline tight.
[11:37] Maya: Noted. we'll aim to deliver final artifacts in Week 6 and schedule the handoff review immediately.
[11:44] Aisha: Thanks all. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[11:47] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the scope doc and calendar invites.
